title: Datacenter Academy: Skills, Jobs and Community Impact
summary: How Microsoft Datacenter Academies are creating pathways to skills and employment in digital infrastructure, using human stories and local examples from multiple markets to demonstrate the long-term community impact of datacenter investment.
body_markdown:
Moénika Hübsch is a current student of the Melbourne program. She grew up gaming, building computers and networks, and attended a technical high school. “I don’t look the part,” she says with a laugh. “But I am a bit of a nerd.” Still, growing up, the message she received from family and close friends was that technology was not a realistic career. “I never thought it was doable for a woman,” she adds.


So after high school she pursued a variety of other career paths – portrait photography, video production, hospitality – before reluctantly retiring for medical reasons.


After rebuilding her health, she decided to finally explore her interest in technology, enrolling in entry-level tech courses at Victoria University with an eye on cybersecurity. That’s when she noticed an ad for Microsoft’s Datacenter Academy on the university website, with critical environment technician classes offered on campus. The opportunity to do something hands-on appealed to her. Today, at 41, she is 4 weeks into a 16-week course that will teach her to work as a critical environment technician, the person responsible for managing the power, cooling and mechanical systems that keep a datacenter running.


The program has reignited her interest in technology and boosted her outlook.


“About two years ago, I was in a wheelchair and relearning to walk with strength and stability without the use a walking stick, so this is so big for me,” says Hübsch. Later this fall, she will apply for a datacenter internship. “I’m going to put my hat in the ring,” she says with enthusiasm. “I’m just so excited about tomorrow.”
